From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Demo booking - calendar shows wrong hour

Hi all — quick technical note from ops side. I dug into the Calendly event metadata for the slot Simon selected. Two things popped up:

1) Calendly event was created with timezone field "America/Los_Angeles" because the browser session reported a US-based locale (likely because Simons IP routed through a corporate proxy when booking). Calendly then emitted an ics with a TZID of America/Los_Angeles, which explains the 5-6 hour shift when Google Calendar interpreted it against Simons local ics settings.

2) Workarounds:
  - The shortest path: well send a manual invite (attached manual-invite.ics) with TZID Europe/London and the attendee times adjusted — please accept that invite and it will replace the mis-timed one.
  - For future bookings, advise the contact to use the Calendly timezone selector (bottom-left of the flow) and confirm it shows Europe/London before confirming.
  - As an internal improvement, Ben is going to add a note on the demo page reminding EU customers to check the timezone selector, and well evaluate forcing explicit timezone detection on the booking page for EU-targeted links.

I attached the manual .ics (manual-invite.ics) and included a one-line script I used to inspect the ics timezone blocks. If you want, Ben can patch the public page copy this afternoon.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
